key_insight: Including solute mass transfer in droplet impact and solidification modeling changes the predicted flow, freezing front, and macrosegregation patterns, leading to better agreement with experiments.
engineering_relevance: This work improves predictive simulation of alloy splat formation, helping engineers anticipate defect-prone segregation zones and cracking risk in thermal spray and additive manufacturing processes.
method: Coupled hydrodynamics, wetting, conjugate heat transfer, phase change, and solute transport in a multiphysics model
Added a concentration-flux-correction algorithm to conserve solute mass at the discrete level
Mapped macrosegregation to identify high-risk regions in the solidifying droplet
evidence_signal: The model was carefully validated across multiple benchmarks and then applied to an alloy droplet impact case, where including mass transfer improved agreement with experimental observations.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate mushy-zone thermodynamics and solute transport resolution, so coarse meshes or simplified phase-change parameters may miss critical segregation features.
paper_title: Numerical Modeling of a Metallic Alloy Droplet Impact, Solidification, and Macrosegregation
